read: The semis liquidation has paused, not reversed. QQQ is -2.1% at 14% of range and flat over 30 minutes. LITE/TER/AVGO/INTC bounced 0.5-1% off the lows, but AMD (-10.9%, 1% of range) and CSCO (2%) are still pinned. Defensives and payments lead. The new headlines are an activist adding to a stake (FISV), an SMCI denial, a Microsoft 365 outage and price-target trims on names that already moved. None of these is a fresh catalyst the price hasn't absorbed, and web search found no same-day primary source (the index lags). No trade. The morning book has no intraday positions to close.

considered.why_not: Jana raised its Fiserv stake 13% to 4.15M shares (11:41). This looks like a holdings disclosure of buying done in Q3, not a new demand. The stock was already +2.8% since open and at 90% of range before the headline, so the news only confirms a move that's already in the price.

Down 10.9%, at 1% of range, still falling (-0.8% in 30 minutes) while peers bounce. That makes it a relative-weakness laggard, and I still can't name the driver, so I can't argue the move is too big. Fading it remains knife-catching.

Three more target cuts since 10:20 (Piper $112, Barclays $109, Wells $130), and it sits at 2% of range. But this is post-earnings recap flow on a stock already -6%; continuation from here is roughly what random names in a weak tape would do.

The 11:46 statement denies Megaspeed was ever a customer and says SMCI cooperated with US, Taiwan and Singapore authorities. The probe it answers is unconfirmed by me, and the stock is -3% alongside semis, so a denial isn't enough to separate it from sector flow.

The Microsoft 365 outage (Outlook, Teams, Copilot) isn't moving the stock, which is flat on the day and +0.6% since open. Past outages haven't changed the earnings view, so there's no trade either way.
